title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
summary: This matching program will support the U.S. Department of Education (ED) and the Department of War (DoW) in meeting the requirements set forth in Section 559(b) of the Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, which requires the Secretary of Education and the Secretary of War to enter into a matching program to identify servicemembers and staff eligible for certain public service loan forgiveness programs. Under this matching program, DoW (source agency) will disclose to the ED, Federal Student Aid (FSA), (recipient agency), information on individuals who, at any time beginning on or after October 1, 2007, were members of the Armed Forces serving on active duty for a period of more than 30 consecutive days or civilian employees of DoW, for the purposes of: (1) identifying whether they made one or more student loan payments eligible to be counted for purposes of the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Program under subsection 455(m) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) and Temporary Expanded PSLF (TEPSLF) program; and (2) without requiring further information from them, certifying the total period of such service or employment for purposes of such program and counting the total number of qualifying payments made by them for purposes of such program during such period. ED will evaluate the information that it receives from DoW to create a count of qualifying payments under PSLF made by covered employees on their respective Title IV Loans (as defined herein). In addition, ED will create customized notifications for covered employees based on the status of their respective Title IV Loans and whether they have already submitted a PSLF and TEPSLF Certification and Application (PSLF form).

title: Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
summary: FinCEN is issuing this proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements under the Customer Due Diligence Rule consistent with the policy goals of, and as directed by, Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System. Specifically, the proposal ensures financial institutions covered by the Customer Due Diligence Rule collect sufficient information to verify the identities of beneficial owners of legal entity customers and maintain the authority, where warranted, to obtain additional information, including information relevant to whether the beneficial owners of legal entity customers possess lawful immigration status and employment authorization in the United States when such information is relevant to assessing risks.

title: Realty Action: Modified Competitive Sale of 20 Parcels of Public Land in Clark County, Nevada; Modification of Recreation and Public Purposes Act Classification
summary: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) proposes to offer 20 parcels of public land, totaling 200.64 acres in the Las Vegas Valley (Valley), by modified competitive sale at no less than each parcel's fair market value (FMV) pursuant to the Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act of 1998 (SNPLMA), as amended. The sale would be processed in conformance with applicable provisions of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (FLPMA) and BLM regulations. A 4.88- acre parcel proposed for inclusion in the sale was previously part of Recreation and Public Purposes (R&PP) Act lease N-75746. At the request of the lessee, the City of Las Vegas, the BLM approved the relinquishment of these acres from the lease. Because the parcel is no longer subject to the R&PP lease, the BLM proposes to modify the R&PP classification by removing the classification from the 4.88-acre portion of the parcel. This modification is necessary because lands that retain R&PP classification are not available for disposal under SNPLMA, and removing the classification makes parcel NVNV106381471 eligible for nomination in the 20-Parcel SNPLMA Land Sale.

title: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke; Notice of Partially Closed Meeting
Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
summary: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

title: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Changes To Support Coordinated Care and Individual Engagement and Reduce Regulatory Burdens
summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or "Department") is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information ("Privacy Rule") under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.

title: Automatic Enrollment Requirements Under Section 414A

The regulations reflect statutory changes made by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 requiring that certain cash or deferred arrangements and salary reduction agreements be eligible automatic contribution arrangements that satisfy additional specified requirements. The regulations affect participants in, beneficiaries of, employers maintaining, and administrators of certain retirement plans that include cash or deferred arrangements or annuity contracts purchased under salary reduction agreements and other retirement plans that include eligible automatic contribution arrangements.
